title: Flip Game
summary: Given a string currentState that consists only of '+' and '-', return all possible resulting states after flipping two consecutive "++" to "--".
statement: Given a string currentState that consists only of '+' and '-', return all possible resulting states after flipping two consecutive "++" to "--". If no valid move is possible, return an empty list.
constraints: Return every state reachable by changing exactly one occurrence of consecutive '++' to '--'. Return unique states in any order; do not modify any other character.
hints: Each legal answer corresponds to one start index where two adjacent characters are plus.
Scan every adjacent pair and construct one new string for each '++'.
For index i, concatenate state[:i], '--', and state[i+2:].
Different start indices change different positions, so their resulting states are unique even for overlapping pairs.
editorial: A single left-to-right scan finds every legal pair. Strings are immutable, so each answer is built from the untouched prefix and suffix around one replacement. Overlapping pairs are separate moves and must both appear. The independent oracle uses the same direct move definition, with exhaustive regression over short binary states.

tests.explanation: Flipping the pair at positions 0, 1, or 2 yields --++, +--+, and ++--.
No two plus signs are adjacent, so there is no legal move.
